plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs time-to-event, adjusted for case/control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question is a single, well-posed survival association: does a per-sample score of the study's 20-gene signature (signature/signature_genes.csv, 20 symbols, no weights) associate with time to event in this 120-sample human tumour-biopsy cohort, after adjusting for case vs control status. The inputs are a raw integer gene-level Salmon count matrix (counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 120 sample columns plus the gene-symbol column) and a 120-row sample table (metadata/metadata.csv) carrying condition, time, and event.

The plan is therefore short and linear, and deliberately does NOT include a genome-wide differential expression or enrichment analysis — the user did not ask for pathways or DE genes, and adding them would be unasked scope that also invites double-dipping.

T1S1 does sample-structure QC on the counts (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) and, critically, reconciles the 120 metadata rows against the 120 count columns and audits the survival columns: how many of the 20 signature symbols are actually present among the 12,000 genes, the number of events vs censored observations overall and within each of the 60 cases and 60 controls, and the median follow-up. The event count, not the sample count, determines the power of everything downstream; with 120 subjects and 2 model terms the rule of ~10 events per parameter is easily met only if there are at least ~20 events, so the audit is what tells us whether the Cox fit is interpretable at all.

T1S2 filters low-count genes with filterByExpr (min_count 10, min samples = smallest group size = 60) and produces TMM-normalised log2-CPM. This is the log-scale matrix the rank-based scorer expects; the counts themselves are never pre-scaled by an ad-hoc factor.

T2S1 computes the per-sample signature score with UCell (rank-based Mann-Whitney U on within-sample ranks, so the score does not depend on library depth or on which other samples are in the matrix), reporting exactly which of the 20 genes were present after filtering. singscore is the named fallback if any signature gene is lost to filtering and an unfiltered-matrix score is preferred. Because the signature is fixed and externally supplied — not selected on these samples — no cross-validation is needed for the score itself; the plan states this explicitly so the scoring step is not confused with a trained classifier. The step also reports the score distribution by condition (a t-test/limma on the scores with the design), which matters because if the score is strongly condition-dependent, the score and the condition covariate will be collinear in the Cox model.

T2S2 answers the question: a Cox proportional-hazards model of Surv(time, event) on the standardised score (continuous, per SD, never dichotomised) with condition as a covariate, reported as HR with 95% CI and Wald p, beside the score-only model so the adjustment's effect is visible. Proportional hazards is checked on scaled Schoenfeld residuals; if it fails, a time-varying effect or stratified model is reported instead of a single HR. Discrimination is quantified with the c-index and time-dependent AUC at horizons chosen from the observed follow-up distribution, with numbers at risk. Kaplan-Meier curves by score tertile are produced for illustration only, with the inference kept in the continuous model. A score x condition interaction is fitted as a secondary, explicitly exploratory test of whether the association differs between cases and controls.

T2S3 writes the report: the primary answer with its uncertainty, the event/censoring accounting, the PH diagnostics, and the reproducibility record. It states plainly that this is a single-cohort, internally-estimated association with no external validation, and that a c-index estimated on the same samples is optimistic.

With 120 subjects and 2 model terms, the model is adequately parameterised provided the event count from T1S1 supports it; the interaction model adds a third term and is correspondingly more fragile.
acceptance_criteria: HR per SD of the signature score with 95% CI and Wald p is reported for the primary score + condition model, beside the unadjusted score-only model
Number of events, number censored, and median follow-up are stated with the results
Scaled Schoenfeld residual test and plot are reported for every model term, and a PH violation triggers a stated alternative (stratified or time-varying) rather than a single HR
Concordance index and time-dependent AUC with CI at explicitly named horizons, with numbers at risk, are reported
Kaplan-Meier curves by score tertile are produced and labelled as illustrative, with the inference resting on the continuous model
The score x condition interaction result is reported and labelled exploratory
constraints: The score enters the model as a continuous, per-SD-standardised term; do not dichotomise or apply an optimised cutpoint before the test
Condition (case vs control) must be in the primary model as a covariate, with the reference level stated explicitly
Report the unadjusted score-only model alongside so the effect of adjustment is visible
Do not perform any feature selection or gene-level screening in this step — the signature is fixed and external
Report the c-index as internally estimated and therefore optimistic; there is no external validation cohort in these inputs
Implement in R (survival is not installed; use rms/riskRegression/survminer/timeROC) or in Python with lifelines and scikit-survival — verify the chosen package imports before writing the model code
caveats: No external validation cohort is present in these inputs. Every performance number (c-index, time-dependent AUC) is estimated on the same 120 samples that fit the model and is optimistic; state this rather than reporting it as validated performance.

If the score is strongly associated with condition (T2S1), the adjusted HR partly removes the very signal of interest and the two terms compete; report the correlation and both models rather than only the adjusted estimate.
A significant interaction term on a cohort this size is exploratory — interaction tests have roughly a quarter of the power of the corresponding main-effect test.

The base R survival package is NOT installed in this environment. rms, riskRegression, pec, timereg, prodlim, survminer, and timeROC are present on the R side, and lifelines 0.30.0 and scikit-survival 0.28.0 on the Python side. Pick one track and verify the import before writing the model.

grounding.reason: A per-sample score against a time-to-event outcome is tested with a Cox model carrying the clinical covariate, the score continuous and per SD, PH checked on scaled Schoenfeld residuals, and the event/censoring/follow-up counts stated (R-0153); discrimination uses time-dependent AUC at stated horizons rather than a plain ROC (R-0156); with no external cohort the performance is reported with the stated caution (R-0154). The package of record, survival, is absent from this environment, so the step names the installed substitutes.

steps.name: Report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the answer to the research question — does the 20-gene signature score associate with time to event once case/control status is accounted for — and with what uncertainty and limitations?
steps.description: Assemble the final report: the primary adjusted hazard ratio per SD of signature score with its CI and p-value, stated first; the event and censoring accounting and median follow-up; the unadjusted comparison; the PH diagnostics and any deviation; discrimination (c-index, time-dependent AUC at the stated horizons) marked as internally estimated; the signature provenance (how many of the 20 genes were scored); the score's relationship to condition; the illustrative KM curves; and the exploratory interaction result. Close with an explicit limitations section covering the absence of any external validation cohort, the absence of clinical covariates beyond condition in metadata.csv (no age, stage, or treatment to adjust for, so residual confounding cannot be excluded), and the event count as the binding constraint on precision. Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo / package versions, the random seed used anywhere randomness enters, and the input file paths with their dimensions.
steps.context: The user asked one question. The report leads with its answer and its uncertainty, and does not dress a single-cohort association up as a validated prognostic biomarker.
acceptance_criteria: The report leads with the adjusted HR per SD, its 95% CI, and p, not with a narrative
Event count, censored count, and median follow-up appear beside the primary result
Limitations explicitly name: no external validation, no clinical covariates beyond condition, internally-optimistic discrimination estimates
Reproducibility record with package versions, seed, and input file paths and dimensions is included
Every figure referenced in the text exists as a written file
constraints: Do not claim clinical or prognostic utility from a single internally-estimated cohort
State the direction of the association in plain terms (higher score = higher or lower hazard) with the reference coding made explicit
If the primary result is null, report it as null — do not substitute the exploratory interaction or a tertile split as the headline
caveats: A tertile KM curve with a striking separation is easy to over-read when the continuous model is null; keep the headline on the continuous model.

grounding.reason: Every report carries the reproducibility record — sessionInfo, package versions, and the seed (R-0086) — and an unvalidated signature carries the stated caution (R-0154).
